placements.why: The document's entire content is about a deployment gate — a mandatory signed-manifest requirement, its scope, its owner, and its incident rationale. No existing strata category exists to hold deployment-process controls; this content names an organizational category that future envelopes about release gates, deployment policies, and pipeline security will feed.
placements.title: organizational controls over what may ship and under what conditions
placements.frame: What mandatory preconditions, ownership assignments, and scope boundaries does the organization impose on its deployment pipelines?

placements.title: a signed release manifest required before any Meridian deployment ships
placements.frame: What makes a deployment gate a non-negotiable precondition rather than a recommendation — and how do scope and ownership ratify it as a settled operational rule?
placements.why: These expressions collectively perform a deployment gate as a settled, load-bearing operational rule: src-1 declares the signed-manifest requirement, src-3 frames what follows as 'Key decisions,' src-4 records the gate, src-5 extends scope to staging and production, and src-6 assigns ownership. The theme — imposing a mandatory process precondition on deployments — is true beyond this specific gate and will accumulate as future envelopes add, modify, or contest deployment gates.

placements.title: a process gate whose whole reason is a prior security incident
placements.frame: When a mandatory process control is justified by citing a past failure, does the incident ground the gate's legitimacy or merely explain it — and does authority-ranking or the precedent carry the weight?
placements.why: src-1 declares the gate from positional authority ('now requires'), while src-2 supplies the factual precedent — two unsigned artifacts reaching staging — as the gate's entire justification ('that is the whole reason for the gate'). The theme — a process control legitimized by citing a prior incident — is a pattern future envelopes will reproduce whenever a new gate or control is rationalized by a past failure, making it a subject beyond this single instance.
